    Decisions to make now

      Details

      Two opposite arms of the MX17 apparatus, which ran at CERN n_TOF in 2026 (a Micromegas TPC, a SiPM scintillator wall and plastic scintillators per arm), sit around a thin Li target and record ⁷Li(p,e⁺e⁻)⁸Be pairs.

      • Why tracking. The opening angle comes from hit positions and cosmic rays are rejected by their straight tracks: the two points at issue in the ATOMKI result (MEG II, 2026).
      • What 8 days deliver. Rates and backgrounds on beam, a calibration on the 441 keV resonance (no anomaly there), and a first look at 18.15 MeV near the ATOMKI level. The results set the design of the four-arm experiment (slot 2).
      • The document. Official LNL template: a one-page abstract and a body of at most 4 pages. Red brackets mark open items; the page plan is in the Proposal tab.
      • This page. Timeline, set-up, beam plan and reach, tasks, budget, risks and questions are in the tabs above. Machine sheet: CN and AN2000 beams ↗.

      The 8 days

      What 8 days can reach

      Geant4, two arms (2026-11-19, lnl_x17/sim2arm/TWO_ARM_STUDY.md): the FEASIBILITY_SIM §19 reference fit (θ × |y| × E_sum, background shape floating) run on one pair of arms of the Cu-hemisphere tables (L11 + L13), with cosmics from every zenith angle (run L15). Range: the two MC-safe estimators. Expected limit = 1.28 / Z(ATOMKI) × R(ATOMKI). The time of flight uses σ_t = 0.6 ns per arm, measured on n_TOF beam-off cosmics (0.52–0.64 ns) with the n_TOF readout. The Al ogive has no two-arm simulation: its rows are the four-arm §19.3 days × the Cu hemisphere's simulated two-arm / four-arm ratio.

      The rules

        What the feasibility run proves

        1 · The apparatus on a proton beam. Trigger and singles rates vs current, DREAM live time, Micromegas occupancy, the Li target's behaviour. Everything the Geant4 reach assumes, measured.
        2 · A calibration at 441 keV. The 17.64 MeV M1 pairs, where ATOMKI saw no anomaly: angular resolution, acceptance and energy scale against Geant4. ~600 selected pairs a day above 90° with two arms: one day is enough.
        3 · The backgrounds. Cosmic nights with the arms vertical before the beam: the 140° cosmic peak MEG II pointed at, measured with and without each veto, and the arm-to-arm time of flight. Accidentals and external pairs with beam.
        4 · A first look at 18.15 MeV. Five days at 1.10 MeV, two opposite arms: an expected 90 % CL limit near the ATOMKI ratio with the liquid cells, ~1.5–2 × without them; MEG II's limit is 2.07 ×. Geant4 (two arms, Cu hemisphere); see Beam & reach.

        Submission and after

        1. INFN-AAI account + "Risorse IT" (do it first; help calcolo@lnl.infn.it).
        2. Online Beam Time Request → report page.
        3. Targets Request Form from the report page.
        4. Keep the confirmation e-mail: it holds the password for changes.
        5. Upload the PDF on Indico before 10 Dec, 23:59 CET.
        • Technical review (internal LNL): beam, target, set-up readiness, radioprotection, safety. Problems sent ~7 days before the PAC (≈ 18 Jan).
        • PAC 25–29 Jan 2027, hybrid. Possible talk: 12 min + 8 min discussion.
        • Then: access registration ≥ 15 d ahead, RP training, dosimeters, a responsibility declaration per shift, a safety data sheet.

        For our planning; the proposal does not need it. Cash only: the Micromegas, walls, plastics, DREAM and most electronics are owned or borrowed. Critical items are what the test cannot run without (B runs with its existing Italian M1 cards). Low-budget upgrades make the run easier to operate; high-budget upgrades look toward the final measurement. Tick items to add them to the selected total. Prices scaled from the MX17 budget (Lean preset) and CAEN offer 26OFC.01101.

        What the two-arm run should see, observable by observable, predicted by the Geant4 simulation before we go: the numbers to check on each night and beam day. Agreement shows the simulation (and so the reach) can be trusted; disagreement says where it is wrong, before the five days at 1.10 MeV. Updated .

        1. Real Geant4 events in the two-arm set-up

        e⁻e⁺ γμ Micromegas segment (pointing line dotted) arm with a trigger leg

        Loading the 3D view…

        Every line is a Geant4 step list (run L17, MX17_Full_Geant lnl_twoarm with --trajdump): the slot-1 geometry with only arms 0 + 1 built (horizontal; arms 2 + 3 for the vertical cosmic nights), the Cu hemisphere with its Li film, the beam line, the as-built stacks (Micromegas, SiPM wall, two plastics, liquid cell). The layer extents are read from the same step points. Events were kept when the analysis would see them (pairs: a leg and a Micromegas track in both arms; γ: a leg in one arm; muons: legs in both) and the drawn ones chosen as typical, not at random: the pairs and muons nearest 140°. Tracks are thinned (e± below 0.1 MeV and γ below 0.2 MeV not drawn). Drag to rotate, scroll to zoom.

        2. The predictions, in the order the run produces them

        Two-arm set-up, Cu hemisphere, 11 µm Li, 1 µA, liquid cells working (“LNL calibrated” response). “× ε” folds in the bench efficiency of each chamber (ε = ); the simulation's chambers are 100 % efficient. MC = number of simulated events behind a number. Rates of 10-hour cosmic nights.

        3. Cosmic nights (before the beam)

        Opening angle of two-track cosmic pairs

        The angle the analysis computes (both Micromegas charge centroids seen from the beam spot), per 10-hour night, log scale. Shaded: the X17 window 125–160°. Vertical arms: the MEG II “140° structure” at full strength.

        Arm-to-arm time of flight

        Δt between the two SiPM walls (vertical: lower − upper; horizontal: −x − +x), with the measured σt = ns per arm. Every vertical muon is downward-going: one peak at +2.3 ns. Beam pairs sit at 0.

        Pointing of the cosmic segments

        Distance of closest approach of one arm's segment to the beam spot, vertical pair: true segment and with 15° (electron-like) and 3° (muon, as on the bench) direction resolution. The cut is mm at 15°, mm at 3°.

        Muon zenith angle

        True zenith angle of the muons making two-track pairs, per night. The two orientations see different muons: near-vertical (vertical pair) and near-horizontal (side arms). The n_TOF A–C pairs (side-by-side arms) had a median of 74°, as the simulation.

        4. Beam singles (day 1: current scan)

        Trigger legs per arm against beam current

        Beam γ (8Be lines) plus cosmics, one side arm. The step from 1.10 MeV to 441 keV is the resonance. The slope is γ yield × leg probability: it measures the film's Li content and the arm's threshold.

        Fraction of legs with a Micromegas track

        Cosmics alone: . Beam singles: . In the simulation, a beam single with a track is a γ that interacted in the Cu hemisphere wall (); one without converted behind the drift gap (readout PCB, support plate, SiPM wall).

        Single-arm energy (legs with a track)

        Energy deposited in one arm (SiPM + plastics + liquid), raw Geant4 deposit before the detector response, per second and MeV at 1 µA, log scale. The beam spectra end near 18 MeV; the cosmic one is a broad MIP sum.

        Rates at 1 µA

        5. Pairs at 441 keV: the calibration (day 2)

        Opening angle, 441 keV

        Selected pairs (pointing + TOF) per 5° bin per day, stacked; error bars: the statistics of the chosen number of days. This is the headline comparison: absolute rate and shape against Geant4, with no free parameter.

        Energy sum and sharing, 441 keV (θ > 90°)

        Esum per 0.5 MeV (after the response) and |y| = |E₁ − E₂|/(E₁ + E₂) per 0.05 in the window, per day.

        6. Pairs at 1.10 MeV (days 3–7)

        Opening angle, 1.10 MeV

        Same selection, per day. On top: an X17 at the ATOMKI ratio, for scale (the run sets a limit, it does not see it at 3σ).
